description: Backend-neutral identity, immutable version, typed and temporal relation, Fact Cut, named ref, compare-and-swap, bounded path proof, and receipt semantics for the Kungfu fact kernel.

logicalId.semantics: Opaque stable identity minted independently from every storage, process, product, and projection coordinate.
logicalId.externalImport: External identities are bound by an explicit mapping receipt; they are not reused as the logical id.

contentRoot.semantics: Immutable identity of exact bytes or an exact canonical record preimage.

identity.separation: A logical id names continuity across immutable versions; no content root, ref name, backend key, or projection coordinate may replace it.

boundaries.authority: An append-only source claim that may precede admission.
A replayable decision binding one observation to exact declarations, policy, outcome, and evidence.
Stable logical continuity independent of any one state or body.
One immutable admitted state of one Fact object with exact body, schema, ancestry, declaration, and admission roots.
One immutable, reproducible state boundary over admitted object versions, active relations, declarations, admissions, Episode frontier, omissions, and conflicts.
A separately identified bounded causal occurrence whose sealed frontier may be referenced by a Fact Cut.
A rebuildable query, storage, language, CLI, GUI, or Git representation of authoritative records.

legacy.rule: Existing roots retain their exact historical preimage and meaning; v1 is never normalized, reserialized, or relabeled as v2.

rootCanonical.migration: A successor Root uses a successor schema and an explicit kungfu.fact.root-mapping-receipt/v1; the receipt binds both protocol labels, roots, and admission Root without claiming byte equality.

rootAlgorithm.unicode: legacy-library-json-spelling; no portability or NFC-enforcement claim

composition.parentCutRoots: Sorted unique set; zero for a root Cut, one for ordinary succession, two or more for an explicit merge-view Cut.
composition.objectVersions: Sorted unique tuples of logical object id and immutable version root; at most one active version per object id.
composition.activeRelationRoots: Sorted unique roots of relation-add records not revoked at this Cut.
composition.declarationRoots: Sorted unique exact declaration roots governing interpretation.
composition.admissionRoots: Sorted unique exact admission-decision roots supporting included versions and relations.
composition.episodeFrontier: Sorted unique tuples of Episode identity, sealed content root, and accepted manifest frame uid.
composition.omissionRoots: Sorted unique content roots of explicit omission descriptors.
composition.conflictRoots: Sorted unique content roots of explicit unresolved-conflict descriptors.

validation: Every referenced root exists and verifies before Cut admission.
Every object version belongs to its declared logical object id.
Every active relation endpoint resolves under the Cut or is explicitly declared external.
Every included version and relation is supported by the pinned declaration and admission roots.
Every omission and conflict is explicit; neither may be silently dropped.
A Cut never mutates after its root is admitted.

relations.add: A typed relation is introduced by one immutable relation-add root.
relations.revoke: Revocation appends a relation-revoke record; it does not delete or rewrite the add record.
relations.cutRule: A relation is active only when its add root is included and no accepted revoke applies at the Cut.
relations.forbiddenInference: A relation never copies identity, state, admission, trust, authority, completion, or another relation to either endpoint.

semantics.identity: Every declaration, relation, supersession, revocation, authority proof, provenance object, query, and receipt has an immutable KFR2 content root.
semantics.direction: A path follows sourceRoot to targetRoot only. Reverse compatibility requires another admitted relation.
semantics.operationScope: A predicate and every authority proof name the exact operations for which they apply.
semantics.transitivity: No path is discovered or inferred. More than one edge is accepted only when the caller supplies the complete ordered path and the predicate declares explicit-bounded composition.
semantics.cut: Validity, supersession, revocation, declarations, active relations, and authority are evaluated at the exact requested immutable Fact Cut.
semantics.history: Supersession and revocation append new rooted facts. They never mutate their subject relation or change the result of an earlier Cut query.
semantics.authority: Each non-governing relation authority requires exactly one operation-scoped authority proof valid at the Cut; zero is missing and more than one is ambiguous.
semantics.receipt: Every accepted or rejected explicit path produces a rooted receipt binding the query, Cut, ordered relation roots, authority proof roots, omissions, and stable outcome.

nonClaims: A path receipt does not assert universal truth or external side effects.
A relation does not transfer identity, trust, authority, admission, or completion.
The bounded verifier is not a mutable central graph, search engine, or inference engine.
A provenance object binds exact roots but does not specialize them into release vocabulary.

refs.meaning: A mutable discoverability name for an immutable Fact Cut root; the name is never Cut identity.

cas.existingExpectedOld: exact current Cut root and exact current revision
cas.idempotency: Replaying the same transitionId with byte-identical input returns the original receipt; reusing it with different input fails.
cas.atomicity: The ref transition and its accepted receipt are one logical append decision.

refs.fork: Create a new ref with expected-old null and a known Cut root; the source ref does not move.
refs.mergeView: Create an immutable Cut with two or more parent Cut roots, then CAS a named ref to it; moving a ref alone never merges state.
refs.rollback: CAS a ref to a known earlier Cut using kind rollback and an explicit reason root; history and intervening Cuts remain intact.
refs.receiptBoundary: A receipt proves the kernel decision and observed ref transition, not external truth, completion, provider durability beyond its declared profile, or distributed consensus.

profiles.admitted: exact requested profile only when every required subpath is qualified
profiles.effective: minimum of content provider, journal sync, and durable-ingest checkpoint
profiles.achieved: returned only from the checkpoint-covered durability receipt; success requires achieved equals requested

contentClosure.rule: Every stored root is verified before admission; declared external roots remain explicitly separate and are never represented as locally durable content.

journalFrontier.pairing: exact record sequence followed by adjacent accepted receipt sequence
journalFrontier.sync: all Fact journal pages plus the journal directory are synchronized before the durable-ingest checkpoint

rocksdb.reason: wal-os-buffered is weaker than durable_group and durable_sync

reconciliation.verifiedCheckpoint: return the original accepted result and receipt only after closure, adjacent journal pair, ref Cut, and revision verify

releaseGate.rule: Fail closed when the durable provenance contract, retained bundle, source closure, provider profile, qualification envelope, clean-runtime replay, or fault evidence drifts.

closedKernelMetadata.rule: Fixed, closed, replay-critical metadata has one typed journal authority.

domainTypedBodies.rule: Open or evolving domain bodies and typed relation attributes retain one registered FlatBuffers owner.

opaqueBodies.rule: Immutable bytes are addressed by SHA-256; paths and backend keys are implementation details.

json.rule: JSON may render contracts, queries, receipts, and diagnostics; it is not a second record authority.

sqliteAndIndexes.rule: Tables, indexes, caches, and GUI stores rebuild from journal and content roots.

compatibility.additiveFields: require a successor schema version unless explicitly excluded from identity by that version
compatibility.rootAlgorithm: a changed preimage or encoding requires a new protocol tag and schema version
compatibility.migration: Import emits mapping and acceptance receipts; it never rewrites old roots in place.
compatibility.backendReplacement: Allowed only when authority scan, roots, CAS outcomes, and receipts remain equivalent.

failureTaxonomy.meaning: A logical id, root, ref name, or transition id is malformed or derived from a forbidden coordinate.
A record or root protocol version is unknown or incompatible.
The referenced Fact object identity has not been admitted.
The immutable Fact version root is unavailable.
A relation add root targeted by a revoke or Cut is unavailable.
A parent, target, or expected-old Fact Cut root is unavailable.
A referenced immutable body is absent from the declared content namespace.
Bytes or canonical record fields do not reproduce the declared root.
Stored bytes fail content verification.
The exact schema owner or schema root required to interpret a body is unavailable.
The body or record cannot be interpreted under the pinned schema version.
A version or relation lacks exact admitted declaration and admission support.
A relation endpoint is absent, ambiguous, or not explicitly external.
The relation has already been revoked under the accepted history.
Cut membership, parents, frontier, omissions, conflicts, order, or uniqueness violates the contract.
A transition for an existing ref omitted exact expected-old root or revision.
The current ref root or revision differs from expected-old; no transition is appended.
A transition id was replayed with non-identical input.
A durable ref operation wrote visible authority but did not return success; callers must reconcile the original operation id without guessing or changing identity.
The provider could not complete the logical append decision under its declared profile.
Authority import stopped after one or more complete logical append decisions; the response identifies the exact committed prefix and same-bundle retry boundary.
The requested durability claim exceeds the active provider's qualified evidence.
The typed KFR2 logical input does not match its closed descriptor shape or canonical transport spelling.
A KFR2 integer exceeds its declared signed or unsigned 64-bit range.
A KFR2 float is NaN or infinity; positive and negative finite zero remain distinct.
KFR2 text is malformed UTF-8, non-shortest UTF-8, or contains a surrogate instead of Unicode scalar values.
A KFR2 set contains two values with equal canonical preimages.
A KFR2 map contains two equal canonical text keys.
A schema-bound KFR2 record contains a field id absent from the closed schema.
A schema-bound KFR2 record repeats one stable field id.
A KFR2 record names a schema absent from the frozen schema registry.
An exact byte or binary64 transport uses malformed or non-lowercase hexadecimal text.
A typed KFR2 input names a value type absent from the frozen protocol.
Absent was supplied as a value even though only a schema may omit a field; null remains an explicit value.

publicQueryBoundary.input: An exact Fact Cut root, or a named ref resolved to an exact Cut root plus ref-resolution receipt.
output: immutable bodies and explicit availability when requested
publicQueryBoundary.headRule: head is syntactic sugar that must resolve to and report an exact ref revision and Cut root.
publicQueryBoundary.projectionRule: Authority scan defines semantics; SQLite, graph, search, GUI, and language projections must prove equivalent roots and visible gaps.
publicQueryBoundary.failureRule: Missing, corrupt, incompatible, omitted, conflicting, or unverifiable inputs remain explicit and cannot be converted into an apparently complete result.

falsifiers.rule: A filesystem path cannot mint or replace a logical Fact object id.
A Git ref or commit cannot replace a Fact Cut root.
A database row or key cannot replace an immutable Fact version root.
A PID, thread, or process lifetime cannot satisfy expected-old CAS.
A GUI route or current screen cannot satisfy expected-old CAS.
Wall clock fields cannot enter Fact Cut identity.
A recorded observation cannot replace an admitted immutable Fact version.
An Episode identity or sealed root cannot replace a Fact Cut root.
A projection row cannot replace journal and content-root authority.
Relations never silently copy state, trust, authority, or another relation.
An existing named ref cannot move without exact expected-old root and revision.
A stale expected-old must fail without a write.
Rollback cannot delete or rewrite Cut or ref-transition history.

nonClaims: The default native writer or the explicit Fact current-hardware candidate is release-qualified for production durability or distributed operation.
A long-term fleet backend is selected.
Distributed consensus, replication, or high availability is provided.
A receipt proves universal external truth or work completion.
Physical-power-loss durability or production eligibility is qualified.
A projection, Git repository, database, process, or GUI is fact authority.
